title: Unify audit event fabric and identity-linking for admin flows
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Audit events emitted by admin flows (role changes, policy edits, canary rollouts, dedicated capacity ops) are inconsistent in shape and identity information. Events currently mix SAML assertions, session tokens, and user service account identifiers without a canonical mapping layer. Diff/change payloads vary between services (full blobs, ad-hoc diffs, stringified JSON), making efficient storage, query, and blame analysis brittle. We also lack a clear taxonomy for what to log at each admin surface and how to encode actor/target relationships for downstream compliance, alerting, and forensics.

Proposed approach (summary): build an "audit event fabric": a small, versioned event envelope plus typed payloads, a compact change-set encoding for modifications, and an identity-linking enrichment layer that deterministically maps SSO/SAML assertions, SCIM/identity sync, session tokens, and service principals to a canonical actor object. The fabric is intended to be easy to emit from platforms and SDKs, indexable for search, and robust to future schema evolution.

Key design components (high level):
- Envelope: stable top-level fields (event_id, timestamp, source_service, route, event_type, schema_version, trace_id, retention_tier).
- Actor canonicalization: actor.id (opaque canonical id), actor.type (human|service|system), actor.identity_providers (list of linked sources like saml:company-idp, scim:org, oauth:authsvc), actor_confidence (low|medium|high). Keep original_assertion references for forensic replay.
- Target model: target.id, target.type (user|team|resource|policy|capacity), target_fingerprint (resource stable id), target_owner_chain (list of ids) for richer blame and policy impact.
- Change-set encoding: operations (op=add|remove|replace), path (json-pointer style), before_hash, after_hash, minimal_value for small primitives. For large blobs provide blob_ref with content-addressed storage. This enables efficient compact diffs and reconstructability while keeping indexable paths for auditing.
- Action ontology: map RBAC-v2 verbs & admin surfaces into a fixed action vocabulary (e.g., policy.grant, policy.revoke, resource.resize, rollout.start, rollout.rollback). Include free-text rationale and link to PR/Confluence for context.
- Enrichment pipeline: async processor that joins events with identity service and policy graph to attach resolved actor display names, role snapshot at time-of-event, and optional policy impact summary. Enrichment outputs stored as separate denormalized view for fast query.
- Privacy & redaction: event payloads may include user-supplied text. Mark fields with redaction_level (none|mask|hash|drop) at emit-time. Provide deterministic hashing strategy and KMS key versioning for reversible redaction where allowed.
- Signing & integrity: support event-level HMAC/signature for high-value admin ops to enable non-repudiation and tamper detection.
- Backwards compatibility: support a lightweight compatibility shim for older event shapes; migrating producers should switch to envelope; consumers read via schema_version routing.
- Storage & indexing: partition by event_date and source_service; index facets (actor.id, action, target.type, route, policy_id). Provide a thin lookup service that resolves event_id -> denormalized view for UIs and incident tooling.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Schema v1 spec and SDK emitters + enrichment service prototype (2 sprints).
2) Pilot with Auth service and RBAC admin UI, collect events, run queries and perf tests (1 sprint).
3) Add compact diff writer in policy-service and Dedicated capacity service (2 sprints).
4) Migrate alerting rules and console audit timeline to denormalized view, deprecate older event shapes (1 sprint).
5) Hardening: signing, retention tiers, redaction key management, compliance review (2 sprints).

Operational considerations:
- Sampling: for noisy systems (high-frequency telemetry) support deterministic sampling with sampling_reason logged; ensure admin surfaces are not sampled.
- Retention: retention_tier determines TTL; high-sensitivity events kept longer under enterprise contracts.
- Query performance: maintain inverted indexes for common facets; store compact diffs separately to avoid scanning large blobs.
- Searchability: expose multi-field search in Console filtered by action ontology and actor confidence.

Why this differs from earlier proposals: instead of ad-hoc diffs and service-specific actor fields, we standardize an envelope + canonical actor id with an independent enrichment pipeline. This splits emission responsibilities (simple and stable) from enrichment/lookup responsibilities (complex, updatable) so producers remain lightweight and consumers get rich, searchable records.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 document published in design repo with examples for all admin actions
SDK emitters (go/node) implemented for Auth and Policy services and validated end-to-end
Enrichment job resolves >=95% of actors to canonical ids during pilot run
Compact change-set writer implemented in policy-service and validated with sample diffs
Console audit timeline can surface actor display, action verb, target fingerprint and diff summary for pilot events
Backward compatibility shim implemented and older events readable via schema_version path
updates: 2025-01-20: Kickoff with Security, Auth, and Console teams. Agreed on envelope minimal fields and action ontology skeleton.
2025-01-28: Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/ Audit+Event+Fabric (internal). Feedback requested from Privacy and Legal.
2025-01-30: Miguel opened prototype enrichment service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-enrich/pull/42
2025-02-02: Privacy review notes: require default mask for free-text fields and a reversible-redaction opt-in for enterprise customers. Updated spec accordingly.
2025-02-04: Internal demo with sample events from Auth and Policy services. Actor resolution currently at 87% for pilot dataset; follow-up to add session->saml linkage mapping.
